The core tension in defensive strategy emerges from the interplay between positional discipline and dynamic ball tracking. Positional discipline (P) is a binary constraint on movement, where deviation leads to catastrophic failure. Ball tracking (B) introduces a probabilistic element through confusion index (C), which quantifies the likelihood of misinterpreting motion. Pass complexity (P_c) acts as a multiplier on defensive load, increasing decision entropy. These primitives form a triadic system: P ⊥ B ⊥ P_c, where each component's failure mode is independent yet collectively deterministic. The epistemic failure occurs when C exceeds threshold, causing P to collapse under uncertainty. The dual nature of the forward pass introduces a non-linear feedback loop: increased offensive capability (R) demands proportional increase in D_t, which may exceed human processing limits. Thus, the system exhibits a phase transition at P_c = 1.2, beyond which defensive coherence fails.
